Well, has it? I know this post is long, but it's an easy and comprehensive read, so go grab a cup of coffee - I know the voat community can handle something longer than a pun.

 

Some may say that the intelligentsia left reddit a long time ago - or, were never even a part of reddit. However, the definition of intelligentsia fits into the voat population, generally and thus far:

"a social class of people engaged in complex mental labour aimed at guiding or critiquing, or otherwise playing a leadership role in shaping a society's culture and politics. This therefore might include everyone from artists to school teachers, as well as academics, writers, journalists and other hommes de lettres (men of letters) more usually thought of as being the main constituents of the intelligentsia"

 

Notice how the definition underscores content makers, something we already see voaters doing, and “class of people… shaping a society’s culture and politics.” We are definitely doing that, in voicing our opposition to the apparent fact that reddit is now the latest victim beholden to the whims of SJW, weekend warriors, radical feminists, and any other group of people who seek to censor with mob and fear tactics. The classic impetus for fleeing intelligentsia, academics, and members of a free society is present: censorship. Youwei, a pseudonym for a scholar based in China (what a nice parallel to doxxing), in his recent article in Foreign Affairs writes of the authoritarian government in China,

"This system for ensuring domestic security is designed to nip any signs of opposition, real or imagined, in the bud. Prevention is even more important than repression - in fact, violent suppression of protests is seen as a sign of failure."

 

Sound familiar? But why the sudden oppression? T.J. Kirk, aka The Amazing Atheist, eloquently entreats his audience to reflect on the atmosphere these groups create, groups ironically more interested in perceived power that actual social justice:

“No one should have to live in fear that the next joke they tell might cost them their livelihood [He says this two years before the tragedy of Tim Hunt]. No one should have to censor themselves 24/7 because people like Adria Richards have been given this de facto, grand inquisitor status, because they know that they have the power to get rid of anything they don’t like simply by pointing at it and saying, ‘I’m offended!’ What about those of us who are offended that our world is being taken over by overly sensitive cry babies who exhibit extremely hypocritical behavior and treat us all like children? What about those of us who are offended by people who presume to dictate what we’re allowed to joke about? What about those of us who are offended by how bland life has become thanks to all these self-appointed thought police running around making a big show of their every indignation?"

 

So, what should we do? Keep voating, keep contributing OC and making comments. Intellectuals remaining in reddit – askScience, history, etc., we call on you to join us in this movement. Harmful Opinions, a games and games media channel that supports consumer action and freedom of expression, suggests a nice way to buck against this ugly trend:

"We are never to get rid of the people who try to pull this shit, without actually being in a bad position, like some people are. So I have an idea; we, the adults who can get along with people, regardless of what they look like or where they come from, should work together to deliberately create a huge societal divide. Forget any divides there may be between genders, races, sexualities - anything like that -whether they’re there or not, and whether they’re significant or not. We are going to create a split so wide that those won’t even be noticeable. We should all cooperate, accepting everyone’s different views, in order to crack society down the middle by a line of people who actually do things, and those who cry."

 

What do you think? Is anyone still on that site truly conscious of what has happened, and doesn’t care despite the zero effort it would take to switch to voat, or at the very least some other social medium? Or have we reached the tipping point, and the exodus will continue until the diaspora is complete? This isn’t about internet points anymore. TL;DR:

First they came for ViolentAcrez, and I did not speak out—because I was not subscribed to /r/creepshots. Then they came for the shitlords, and I did not speak out— because I was not subscribed to /r/fatpeoplehate. Then they came for the Victoria Taylor, and I did not speak out—because I was not subscribed to /r/ama. Then they came for my subreddit —and there was no one left to speak for me.
